prompt: Fastify's Content-Type parser (the ContentType class in lib/content-type.js) mishandles quoted parameter values (RFC 9110 quoted-string): a ';' inside quotes ends the value early, a 'key=value' inside a quoted value leaks out as a separate parameter, and backslash escapes are not unescaped. Fix it so a parameter value may be a token or a full quoted-string, and inside a quoted-string ';', '=' and escaped quotes are part of the value. For a quoted value, remove the surrounding double quotes and replace every backslash-escaped character (\x) by the character itself. Examples: 'application/json; name="foo;bar"; charset=utf-8' is valid, with media type 'application/json', parameter name 'foo;bar' and charset 'utf-8'; 'application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"; boundary=xyz' is valid with name 'a=b;charset=fake', boundary 'xyz' and no charset parameter; 'application/json; name="he said \"hi\""' is valid with name 'he said "hi"'; 'application/json; charset="utf-8"; foo="BaR"' still gives charset 'utf-8' and foo 'BaR' (case preserved). Because reply.send relies on this parser to see whether a charset is already declared, a reply with Content-Type 'application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"' sending { hello: 'world' } must be sent with Content-Type 'application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"; charset=utf-8'.
requirement: ContentType parameter values follow RFC 9110: parameter-value = token / quoted-string; inside a quoted-string, qdtext (including ';' and '=') and quoted-pairs are part of the value; the stored value has the DQUOTEs removed and each quoted-pair replaced by its octet. Parameter names are lowercased; values keep their case. A quoted value never yields extra parameters. reply.send appends '; charset=utf-8' when no real charset parameter is present, even if a quoted value contains 'charset='.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 'application/json; name="foo;bar"; charset=utf-8' is valid with mediaType 'application/json', name 'foo;bar' and charset 'utf-8'
'application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"; boundary=xyz' is valid with name 'a=b;charset=fake', boundary 'xyz' and no charset parameter
a quoted-pair is unescaped: name="he said \"hi\"" gives 'he said "hi"'
'application/json; charset="utf-8"; foo="BaR"' gives charset 'utf-8' and foo 'BaR'
reply.send with Content-Type 'application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"' sends 'application/json; name="a=b;charset=fake"; charset=utf-8'

adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit.

provenance.author: Claude (QB developer side; dev screen, harder candidates)
provenance.notes: Real defect in fastify v5.10.0 (quoted-string parameter values split on ';' and not unescaped), fixed upstream in 29bdcbb9 (#6865). The reference is that fix applied to v5.10.0; the hidden suite is the upstream tests plus the preserved quoted-value case.
